steps.title: About this project
steps.narration: Why I built this site: class readings on Sherald, Hill, and Jacobs showed Black women's interior lives getting reduced to respectability performance or silence.

steps.title: What She Did Not Say
steps.narration: Thesis: dissemblance hid interior life under surveillance; respectability was its public face. Michelle Obama's portrait and the labor-force chart anchor the claim in image and data.

steps.title: Argument summary
steps.narration: Shield (Hine), cage and key (Higginbotham), refusal (Davis, Combahee, Sharpe)—three claims to test against each photograph and source.
suggestedQuestions: Summarize the thesis in three sentences.
What are shield, cage, and refusal?

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: Whose interior can history see when courts read composure as consent? Hine's shield and Higginbotham's respectability are the two lenses.

steps.title: Antebellum: Jacobs and the garret
steps.narration: Jacobs hid seven years above her enslaver's store, then published. Miles's sack and Painter's soul murder show what archives miss when they record property, not interior life.
suggestedQuestions: How does the garret illustrate dissemblance?

steps.title: Freedom: Walker, clubs, and NACW
steps.narration: After emancipation: washerwomen strikes, Walker entrepreneurship, Burroughs schools, and NACW club growth—respectability as leverage inside Jim Crow.
suggestedQuestions: What does the NACW chart show?

steps.title: Timeline
steps.narration: Sixteen dates from Truth's birth to Sherald's 2024 retrospective. Each card links one event to visibility, labor, or testimony.
suggestedQuestions: What happened in 1892 on the timeline?

steps.title: Activism: Wells and the lynching script
steps.narration: Wells printed names and dates against lynching apologias. She calibrated tone for readers trained to punish Black women for sounding too angry or too calm.

steps.title: Blues legacies
steps.narration: Davis reads blueswomen naming desire and violence uplift sermons smoothed over. Larsen and Hall's Passing update dissemblance for fiction and film.
suggestedQuestions: How do blues relate to dissemblance?

steps.title: Civil rights and Black feminism
steps.narration: Tougaloo Nine, natural hair, McGuire on assault testimony, Baker's organizing, Combahee, Lorde on anger—four pressures on what Black women could say aloud.
suggestedQuestions: What is the Combahee River Collective?

steps.title: Contemporary credibility traps
steps.narration: Undertreated pain, adultified Black girls, Anita Hill and #MeToo, Sherald and Say Her Name—visibility without belief or repair.
suggestedQuestions: What is the Say Her Name frame?

steps.title: Conclusions
steps.narration: Shield, cage, refusal—then five quoted voices. When a source sounds too neat, check the gap between performance and interiority.

steps.title: Sources
steps.narration: Bibliography, chart data (Goldin, Census, BLS), and image credits with licenses.
